prompts.prompt: Before I send docs/order-service-design.md to review, fact-check it. Check its claims against the code in src/ and the load-test data in perf/. Write an accuracy report to accuracy-report.md. Do not edit the design doc. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill makes the reviewer extract every verifiable claim, refuse the document's own word as evidence, classify each claim with a fixed taxonomy and severity, and pair each wrong claim with a correction and source. Without it, reviews tend to spot-check the obvious claims, accept 'AWS recommends' and 'well known' assertions, and skip verified claims or corrections.

floor_checks.text: Refutes the 10,000 RPS claim with the measured ceiling from perf/results.csv

rubric.criterion: Contradicted implementation and data claims are caught with file evidence
rubric.pass: All four are marked Inaccurate with the file that contradicts them: 10k RPS (perf/results.csv peaks near 2,310), retry (src/retry.js is a single try), auth (src/auth.js decodes without signature check), parameterized SQL (orderRepo.search concatenates input)
rubric.partial: Two or three of the four
rubric.fail: One or none, or claims accepted on the doc's word

rubric.pass: Notes at least one of: notifyBilling in src/client.js bypasses withRetry (so 'every outbound call' is false even if retry existed), or the 10,000 target run had a 48% error rate and 9.1 s p99

rubric.criterion: Approach and authority claims are not taken on trust
rubric.pass: The 'AWS recommends / well known exactly-once' claim is Unverifiable or Inaccurate (outbox plus stream is at-least-once) and needs a docs citation; the one-sprint rollout is Overstated because the 'already built' parts are not built
rubric.partial: One of the two handled correctly

rubric.pass: 400 KB DynamoDB item limit and 15-minute Lambda limit are classified Verified, not listed as problems
rubric.partial: Listed with hedging or as low-severity issues

rubric.pass: Summary with total and per-class counts using Verified/Inaccurate/Overstated/Unverifiable/Missing Context, findings grouped High/Medium/Low, and original text + corrected text + source for each Inaccurate or Overstated claim
rubric.partial: Most of that structure but missing counts or corrections
rubric.fail: Free-form notes with no classification or corrections

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Evidence cited from the repo, not assertion
Corrections a writer could paste in

prompts.prompt: Our design review is Thursday. Check whether docs/export-design.md will actually work as written, using the code in src/ and the timings in perf/. Write your findings to export-accuracy.md. Do not edit the design doc. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: Step 4 of the skill traces the execution path end to end and flags any step that assumes an unconfirmed capability; its guidelines say service limits must be checked against current documentation. Without it, a reviewer tends to check the individual sentences and miss that a synchronous API Gateway plus Lambda request cannot return a 1.2 GB file or run for minutes.

rubric.pass: States that the synchronous request path cannot carry a 1.2 GB response or a multi-minute run, citing the relevant limits (API Gateway REST 29 s integration timeout and 10 MB payload, Lambda 6 MB sync response) or explicitly marking them to verify in current AWS docs
rubric.partial: Says large exports may time out but without tying it to the request path or any limit
rubric.fail: Does not question the synchronous design

rubric.criterion: The 'already streams to S3' claim is refuted from the code
rubric.pass: Marks it Inaccurate citing src/exporter.js: builds the whole CSV in memory and writes to /tmp, no S3 or multipart call
rubric.partial: Notes exporter.js differs but not how

rubric.criterion: Sizing and timing claims are checked against perf/export-timings.csv
rubric.pass: Shows 40 s is only the medium-tier median (large tier p50 212 s, p95 610 s, max 1,480 s) and that /tmp defaults to 512 MB unless configured, so both claims are Overstated or Missing Context

rubric.criterion: No false positives on the true or unknowable claims
rubric.pass: Scheduler retry is acknowledged as real (3 attempts in src/scheduler.js) with the caveat that the on-demand path never calls it; rate limiting is Unverifiable rather than Inaccurate; limits not found in the repo are not stated as certain facts without a source or hedge
rubric.fail: Calls the retry code nonexistent, or invents evidence

rubric.criterion: Gives a usable correction and alternative
rubric.pass: Proposes corrected text and a workable path (e.g. async job writing to S3 with a presigned download URL, Lambda ephemeral storage or streaming upload), and corrects the 'no new infrastructure, one week' plan

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Did it trace the whole request path?
Code and data cited for each verdict
A fix the team could adopt

prompts.prompt: A reviewer left one comment on docs/order-service-design.md: 'I don't buy the auth section.' I need to reply to them and decide whether the doc needs more work before re-review. Check it against src/ and perf/ and write reply.md with your reply and recommendation. Do not edit the design doc. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill applies the full claim-extraction workflow when a reviewer flags a factual concern, so the reviewer's single comment becomes a check of every claim. Without it, an answer usually confirms the auth problem and stops, sending the doc back for re-review with the throughput, retry and SQL-injection claims still wrong.

rubric.criterion: Confirms the reviewer's concern with evidence
rubric.pass: Shows src/auth.js decodes the JWT payload without verifying the signature, so 'requires only configuration' is Inaccurate and the work is not just setting an issuer URL
rubric.partial: Agrees with the reviewer but without the code evidence
rubric.fail: Disagrees with the reviewer or does not check auth.js

rubric.criterion: Checks the rest of the document, not only the flagged section
rubric.pass: Also reports the other contradicted claims (throughput, retry, parameterized SQL) and classifies them
rubric.fail: Only the auth section is checked

rubric.pass: Says the doc is not ready, lists the corrections needed (with corrected wording or what must be built), and notes the rollout estimate depends on them
rubric.partial: Says it needs work without specifics
rubric.fail: Says it is ready after an auth tweak

rubric.pass: Short, factual reply to the reviewer; does not flag the 400 KB or 15-minute limits as wrong
rubric.partial: Accurate but long or partly off-topic
rubric.fail: Contains incorrect claims or flags true statements as false

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Does it confirm the reviewer with evidence?
Does it stop the doc going back with other false claims?
